newsitem.title: GREECE: FORMER U.S. DEFENCE CHIEF VISITS INTRACOM.
newsitem.headline: FORMER U.S. DEFENCE CHIEF VISITS INTRACOM.

text.p: Former U.S. defence secretary Caspar Weinberger visited Intracom's facilities in Paiania and had talks with its board chairman Socrates Kokkalis, the company said in a statement.
Discussions focused on post Cold War Europe, information technology opportunities in the Balkans and the comparative advantages of Greek firms for further involvement in the area.
"I was very satisfied with my visit at Intracom and the talks with Mr Kokkalis and his associates," Weinberger was quoted as saying after a tour of the company's plant.

"There's no doubt that Greece has a high technology facility of international standards. This is why I will reiterate that Greece can and must become a strong factor of stability and development in the eastern Mediterranean and the Balkans," he said.
Weinberger invited Kokkalis to New York for further contacts with information technology bussiness leaders.
Weinberger, defence secretary under President Ronald Reagan from 1981-87, led the largest peace time armament programme in the U.S. which reached 2.0 trillion dollars, Intracom said.
Born in San Fransisco in 1917 he is presently the president of publishing house Forbes.

Intracom is Greece's largest telecommunications manufacturer with significant international activities. It has developed knowhow in turn-key information technology projects, energy and defence applications. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
